summary: ASML is dutch company and supplier of photolithography systems, founded in 1984. Type: listed company. About 44,027 employees (Wikidata). Revenue Q4916 32.7 billion (2025). Recognised visa sponsor (IND). 98% of its 54 jobs here don't ask for Dutch. News, last 3 months: 6 about funding; 1 about acquisitions; 9 about growth or hiring; 3 about legal trouble, strikes or bankruptcy.

insights.one_liner: Veldhoven-based maker of the machines used to print microchips, with about 44,000 staff; 63 open roles here, 98% in English and 20 internships.

culture.text: Its Veldhoven headquarters is home to more than half of all employees, and 61 of its 63 open roles here are there.
Most staff studied at TU/e, Fontys, TU Delft, Tilburg or Avans, in mechanical or electrical engineering, physics, business or computer science.
Not only engineers: current openings span hardware, operations and supply chain, legal and compliance, IT and finance.
Says it has over 40,000 employees from 143 nationalities across more than 60 locations.

open.text: ASML Holding N.V. and ASML Netherlands B.V. are IND recognised visa sponsors.
98% of its 63 jobs here don't require Dutch, and a quarter mention visa or relocation support.
Of the current openings, 20 are internships, the largest single level.

growth.text: Grew from 23,219 staff in 2019 to 44,027 in 2024, with 43,520 listed for 2026, so growth has levelled off.
Made €32.7 billion revenue and €9.6 billion net profit in 2025.
Named with VDL and NXP as companies in Eindhoven eager for staff, as the region works to train more technical MBO talent.
Land is being expropriated for the ASML expansion area despite last resistance from owners.

worth_knowing.text: The US is pushing for faster export restrictions on ASML, now also targeting machines already installed in China.
Geopolitics is reaching the ASML work floor, according to a local report.
CEO Christophe Fouquet has also taken a supervisory board seat at Airbus.
